newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AUSTRALIA SEMIS - QTC concludes supply for now.
newsitem.headline: AUSTRALIA SEMIS - QTC concludes supply for now.

text.p: TCV NSW T-CORP QTC
SAFA WATC TASCOR
*Last week's QTC bond offering is likely to conclude tender supply on to the semis market for some weeks.
*QTC also tapped dual currency samurai market.

Last week's bond offering by Queensland Treasury Corp (QTC) is likely to conclude tenders on the semis market for some weeks with the other regular tenderer, Treasury Corp of Victoria, having gone in late January.

QTC issued A$100 million of its September 2007 bond, which fetched an average weighted yield of 7.603 percent after a tightly bid contest and came in some 23 basis points over the Australian Treasury's October 2007 bond.
The spread between the two stocks has narrowed to around 22 from 23 basis points in the past week.
QTC also tapped the dual currency samurai bond market with a three-year transaction in the past week, issuing 10 billion in yen, which will redeemable in U.S. dollars.
Issues in these structures have switched to higher-yielding U.S. and New Zealand dollars, and sterling issues and away from Australian dollars, which dominated such activtity during 1996.

"In the current environment, samurai issues with sterling, NZD and USD component are likely to to prove more atractive to retail investors. These currencies are dominating new samurai issues and are likely to pick up a useful share of maturing AUD issues," analysts at Colonial State Bank said in a report.

Colonial estimate that around 1.9 trillion yen of Australian dollar redeemable dual currency samurai bonds were issued in 1996, up from 300 billion yen in 1995, but the reduction in Australian interest rates in the second half of 1996 saw reduced interest in this style of offering.

The first Australian dollar dual currency samurai bonds start maturing in the coming weeks, however they will start to gather pace in October and November 1997 with a preponderance of maturities from February 1998.
This switch away from Australian dollar linked samurais will remove one pillar of support from the currency.
Traders said such supply last year had also benefitted the short-end of the semis curve due to the swap related activity associated with this type of issuance.

Meanwhile, the focus for the Australian market this week will be on Thursday's labour force report after last week's quarterly wages report came in at the top end of expectations and dampened hopes of a further imminent easing official interest rates.
The Australian Treasury is also holding a A$900 million two tranche bond tender on Tuesday.
